info.title: govhub relay API
info.description: A queue in front of a dashd. Accepts fully signed masternode governance FUNDING votes and broadcasts them with `voteraw`, immediately or at a client-chosen release time (deferred / randomized voting), and submits proposals whose collateral is already confirmed. The relay holds no accounts, keeps no IP addresses at rest and only a coarse receive hour per vote. Its operator can see the IP and timing of every request: public unlinkability only. Votes are signed by the client with the masternode VOTING key (`signVote` in @govhub/verify); the relay never sees a key. The id returned by POST /v1/votes, not the vote hash, is the handle for status and cancel. CORS is open (origin *, GET/POST/OPTIONS, header content-type). Every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Every POST body is limited to 4096 bytes (413). Errors are `{error, code}` with a stable `code`.

get.description: Always 200 while the process serves HTTP (container health check). `core.reachable` says whether dashd answers; the answer is cached for 5 s.

post.description:
Checks, in this order: network (`wrong-network`), field types and unknown keys (`bad-request`), Core's relay rules via `relayVoteError` (`bad-vote`: funding only, outcome yes/no/abstain, time positive and at most MAX_HOLD_S ahead), the release time (`bad-release`; a signed `time` older than MAX_PAST_S, default 24 h, is `stale-vote`), the masternode (`unknown-mn`, `mn-banned`), the signature (`bad-signature`: the recovered key must be the masternode's current voting key; Core's non-strict recovery rules, i.e. any header byte and high-S), the proposal (`unknown-proposal`, `not-a-proposal`). A vote whose hash is already stored (in any state) returns 200 with the stored record. Then Core is asked (`gobject getcurrentvotes`; a failing call is ignored): 409 `already-current` if Core already has this vote hash as the masternode's current vote, 409 `newer-vote-in-core` if it has a funding vote of this masternode dated at or after this one; neither is queued or counted against any limit. A held vote of the same masternode on the same proposal is superseded by one with a greater `time` and refused otherwise (`later-vote-held`). Then the limits, which only votes that are really queued count against: per masternode per rolling hour (`rate-limited`), held votes per masternode (`too-many-held`) and held votes in total (503 `relay-full`, MAX_HELD_TOTAL). The per-IP token bucket (`rate-limited`, Retry-After) applies to every POST before the body is read.

The vote is released at `releaseAt` (default: max(now, time - RELEASE_MARGIN_S)); an explicit `releaseAt` must satisfy time - 3540 <= releaseAt <= time + 86400 and releaseAt <= now + MAX_HOLD_S, and a value in the past means now.

200.description: this exact vote (same vote hash) is already stored; its current record

post.description: `sig` is the masternode's CURRENT voting key signing (Dash `signmessage`, DarkCoin message magic, the same scheme on every network) the text `govhub-relay-cancel-v1\n<network>\n<vote hash, lowercase display hex>` (relayCancelMessage in @govhub/verify). A held vote becomes `cancelled`; cancelling a cancelled vote is a no-op 200. A `maybe-broadcast` vote is 409 `maybe-broadcast` with a `reason` the client can show: Core may already have it, so it cannot be taken back. Any other state is 409 `not-held` with the vote's `status`; `sending` (voteraw in flight) is one of them.

409.description: `not-held`: the vote already left the held state. `maybe-broadcast`: an earlier attempt may have reached Core, so the vote cannot be cancelled; `reason` says so in plain words

reason.description: `maybe-broadcast` only: a sentence for the user

get.description: Votes in a final state are deleted RETENTION_DAYS after they finished; the id is then unknown.

get.summary: Status of a submitted vote, by its vote hash
get.description: For a client whose POST /v1/votes got no answer (a timeout), so it never learned the relay id: the same view as GET /v1/votes/{id}, the relay `id` included. 404 `unknown-vote` when this relay holds no vote with this hash (it never received it, or purged it RETENTION_DAYS after it finished). Rate-limited per client like the POSTs: anyone who can guess a vote can compute its hash.

post.summary: Submit a proposal to Core (`gobject submit`)
post.description: 501 `disabled` when the relay runs with PROPOSAL_SUBMIT=0. Everything is verified again before Core is asked: the proposal data (`validateProposalData`, `bad-proposal`), the gov hash, and the collateral transaction fetched from Core (`checkCollateralTx` against that hash and the named txid, `bad-collateral`). A collateral with fewer than MIN_COLLATERAL_CONFS confirmations is 425 `collateral-unconfirmed` with the current `confirmations`. Core's refusal is 409 `core-rejected` carrying Core's message (proposal data is public).

425.description: the collateral transaction is not deep enough yet

Hash.description: lowercase hex in display (RPC) byte order; uppercase is accepted in requests

VoteId.description: 16 random bytes; the handle for status and cancel

VoteStatus.description: `sending`: `voteraw` is in flight right now (a few seconds at most); the vote cannot be cancelled and ends as `broadcast`, back as `held` / `maybe-broadcast` (retry) or `failed`. `maybe-broadcast`: waiting to be sent again like `held`, but an earlier attempt may already have reached Core (voteraw got no answer, the relay restarted mid-call, or a broadcast vote never showed up and is re-sent); it can never be cancelled and never goes back to `held`. Clients must treat unknown statuses as non-final.

network.description: must equal the relay's CORE_NETWORK; it also selects the vote signature scheme (testnet: hash scheme, everything else: message scheme)

signal.description: other signal names are refused with `bad-vote`

time.description: the signed nTime, unix seconds; at most MAX_HOLD_S (default 40 days) ahead of the relay's clock

sig.description: base64 of the 65-byte compact signature (the `voteraw` vote-sig argument)

releaseAt.description: unix seconds. Default max(now, time - RELEASE_MARGIN_S). Must satisfy time - 3540 <= releaseAt <= time + 86400 and releaseAt <= now + MAX_HOLD_S
effective release time, unix seconds (never earlier than the submission)

sig.description: base64 of the 65-byte `signmessage` signature over the cancel message

broadcastAt.description: when Core last accepted the vote from this relay

confirmedAt.description: when the vote was seen in `gobject getcurrentvotes`

attempts.description: voteraw calls that were answered (not counting `too-often` waits)

nextAttemptAt.description: held and maybe-broadcast votes: the earliest time (unix s) the relay sends it; null in every other state

holdReason.description: held and maybe-broadcast votes: why it waits. `release-time`: the client-chosen release; `one-change-per-hour`: Core accepts one change per masternode, proposal and signal per hour; `core-time-limit`: Core refuses votes timed more than 1 h ahead; `retrying`: after an error (see `lastError`). null in every other state

sameAsCurrent.description: at submission, the masternode's current funding vote in Core had the same outcome: broadcasting this one only moves the timestamp (flagged, not dropped). null: Core could not be asked

lastError.description: a short code, never a raw Core message. While held (or `sending`): `too-often` (Core said voting too often), `hour-rule` (this relay broadcast a vote of the masternode on the proposal less than 1 h + 30 s ago), `future-limit` (the signed time is more than 1 h ahead of Core's clock), `unknown-proposal`, `core-error`, `not-visible` (re-broadcast pending). When failed: `obsolete`, `mn-gone`, `mn-banned`, `mn-not-valid`, `bad-signature`, `unknown-proposal`, `core-error`, `unconfirmed`

time.description: the `time` of the governance object (part of its hash)

dataHex.description: proposal JSON as hex, at most 512 bytes

govHash.description: computed by the relay with governanceObjectHash
